reason: The ordering and the quote are exact: ArenaResetService.java:312-314 calls despawnOwnShopNpc(world) (step 7) and :318 calls definitions.clearDeploymentData(arenaId) (step 8), and no step in between or later restores the entity. Nothing on the abort/reinstate path re-spawns it either: abort() -> reinstateRestoring() -> reinstate() -> multi.enableArena() (ArenaResetService.java:457-459, 501-527) only re-queues the arena, and processEnableQueue's new ArenaInstance (MultiArenaManager.java:387) never calls spawnNpc; repo-wide, spawnNpc's only call sites are NpcManager.java:86/301, SetupWizard.java:1031/1320 and HilltopCommandHandler.java:1189. Step 8 genuinely can fail with the registry still populated (ArenaManager.java:719-723 returns false on an unusable load, :750-753 on a failed write; YamlFileGate.java:88-98 returns false on IOException), so the asymmetry is real, not dead code. But the impact is overstated on two counts: (a) a startup-latched read-only arenas.yml cannot reach this path at all, because ArenaManager.load() clears the registry (:135-140) and canReset then answers ARENA_NOT_FOUND (:183-187) - only a mid-session corruption or an IO error makes step 8 fail after step 7; and (b) the claim that the NPC 'only comes back after a full server restart' is false - respawnFromConfig on restart is one of three heals, alongside /hilltop deploy setshop (HilltopCommandHandler.java:1189 spawns the entity before the write that may fail, so it repairs the NPC even while the gate is read-only) and the setup wizard's step-7 shot (SetupWizard.java:1031). What remains is a real ordering flaw: under an already-degraded write path, the arena is reinstated playable with a silently missing plugin-level shop and no log or outcome marker for the removed entity (Outcome.shopNpcCleared is gated on dataCleared at :560, so it stays false). That is a recoverable, one-command-to-fix operational defect in a failure branch, not a medium-severity data or availability bug.
